title: Identity and Equality
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of identity and equality in a Swift program or workflow.
Apply value equality in a small, inspectable example.
Check the expected result and identify one boundary case or platform constraint.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on identity and equality and the practical choices around it. Start with the smallest example, connect it to “Value equality”, and verify the result before adding complexity.
content.why_it_matters: Reusable functions and precise data models reduce duplication. Handling missing data and failures explicitly makes later application code safer to change.

content_blocks.title: Value Types and Reference Types
content_blocks.alt_text: The comparison distinguishes value types, where assignment creates an independent value, from classes, where multiple references can point to the same instance.
content_blocks.caption: Choose copy semantics or shared object identity deliberately.

content_blocks.text: **Start with the rule.** For value equality, identify the contract, the valid inputs, and the failure or boundary case. Write the smallest reusable Swift example that makes those decisions visible.

**Work through the lesson.** Reason about copies, identity, ARC, object lifetime, and the boundary between safe and unsafe memory access. The detailed subtopic list in this lesson preserves the curriculum coverage; treat each item as a cue for a small example or a focused question rather than trying to memorize syntax.

items.title: Identity comparison with classes
items.text: Classes provide reference identity and support inheritance. Shared references require clear ownership and lifetime rules to avoid unexpected mutation or retained objects.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every Swift snippet can run in a browser or on every operating system.
common_mistakes.why: CodeLeaf’s current preview is not a Swift compiler, and Apple frameworks require appropriate target support.
common_mistakes.fix: Run command-line examples locally; use Xcode or a compatible package/target for framework-specific material.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating an illustrative output as compiler verification.
common_mistakes.why: A reference result helps reason about behavior but cannot replace compiling and testing the exact code.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the example with the stated toolchain and test one realistic edge case.

common_mistakes.why: Swift concurrency checks and newer APIs can vary by language mode and toolchain.
common_mistakes.fix: Read the exact diagnostic and confirm the supported version before changing safety checks.
